question_text:
O is the centre of a circle of radius $32\text{ cm}$. Chord [AB] is $50\text{ cm}$ long.
Find:

subparts.solution:
Let $A\hat{O}B = \theta \implies B\hat{O}M = \frac{\theta}{2}$

In triangle OMB, $\sin\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{25}{32}$
$\frac{\theta}{2} = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{25}{32}\right)$
$\theta = 2\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{25}{32}\right)$
$\theta \approx 1.79\text{ radians}$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord and the central angle. The sine ratio in the right-angled triangle gives half the angle.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Calculating the answer in degrees instead of radians.

subparts.stem: the area of the shaded segment.

mark_breakdown.desc: Subtract triangle area from sector area to get $419\text{ cm}^2$

subparts.solution:
$\text{Sector area} = \frac{1}{2}\theta r^2 \approx \frac{1}{2}(1.79)(32)^2 \approx 918.19\text{ cm}^2$

$\text{Triangle area} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\sin\theta \approx \frac{1}{2}(32)^2\sin(1.79) \approx 499.37\text{ cm}^2$

$\text{area of shaded segment} = \text{sector area} - \text{triangle area}$
$\approx 918.19 - 499.37$
$\approx 418.81$
$\approx 419\text{ cm}^2$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The area of a circular segment is the difference between the sector area $\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$ and the triangle area $\frac{1}{2}r^2\sin\theta$, with $\theta$ measured in radians.
step_by_step: Compute the triangle area: $\frac{1}{2} \times 32^2 \times \sin(1.79\text{ rad}) \approx 499.37\text{ cm}^2$.
Subtract the triangle area from the sector area: $918.19 - 499.37 = 418.81\text{ cm}^2$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Evaluating $\sin(1.79)$ with the calculator in degree mode instead of radian mode.
